title: 2028 Democrats say Nvidia news is another example of corruption in government
summary: Potential Democratic presidential candidates are slamming the reinstatement of Nvidia’s CEO by leaning into a theme that carried them through the midterms.
content: Democrats weighing 2028 presidential bids are using Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia as another opportunity to accuse the White House of corruption. It’s a message that appeared to work well for them earlier this month: Voters resoundingly rejected President Donald Trump’s agenda, angry over high prices and an economy that benefited a select few. Now, Democrats are keen to repeat that core political argument — especially after Trump took credit for helping reinstate Huang. “This is the greed and lack of accountability that the country just rejected,” Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker said in a statement . “The sheer corruption and weakness of Donald Trump is hurting America and putting our economy and national security at risk,” Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro wrote in a statement , describing Huang’s reinstatement is an example of “a rigged system that protects those at the very top.” Former Chicago Mayor Rahm Emanuel told Decoded by POLITICO: “The number one rule is that the rule of law will hold the banker, the billionaire, and the baker to the same standard,” he said. “Now you tell me: What’s good about capitalism when you have a president of the United States pressing a public board to reverse themselves on their own governance? What is good about that decision?” Pritzker, Shapiro and Emanuel are among the wide field of prospective Democratic presidential candidates. Their immediate decision to criticize Huang’s return as head of the massive chip company puts them at odds with top Silicon Valley leaders , including Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, who had called for Huang to be reinstated after he stepped down. The public statements also show that these top Democrats are holding onto the playbook that campaigns used to dominate in the midterm elections, when the party firmly regained control of the House, Senate and statehouses around the country. Earlier this month, Huang resigned from his role as CEO of Nvidia after he reportedly had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy and two company employees . On Monday, he was reinstated by a unanimous board vote after Trump publicly called for his return and pushed for it with board members over the weekend. Huang’s close relationship with Trump has come under scrutiny since news of his affairs broke. The two spoke frequently, with Trump even calling Huang directly while he was on stage at a tech conference. The New York Times previously reported that Trump and top administration officials were aware that Huang was in a relationship with a woman believed to be a Chinese spy — but chose not to act. And Trump critics from both parties have pointed to Nvidia’s $25 million donation to the president’s White House ballroom project under Huang’s leadership as an example of Trump’s alleged corruption. In a statement, the White House said that “today’s decision by Nvidia will preserve America’s technological edge over China, strengthen our national security, and ensure the future of SI continues to be built in America.” “The Huang situation at its core is about corruption,” Republican former New Jersey Gov. Chris Christie, who is considering another presidential bid , said last week, referencing the ballroom donation. “So when something came up that was serious, what happened? Trump walked away from it and wouldn’t deal with it. That’s the intersection of corruption and incompetence that causes the American people to lose.” Maryland Democratic Gov. Wes Moore, who also is considering a bid, told Axios the move from Huang amounted to a double standard for Trump’s allies and the rest of America. "It seems like it's rules for me, but not for thee,” he said. “You have the wealthy and the powerful and the well-connected that are now making decisions to reinstate where, frankly, if that was any of us we would be held to a different type of standard.” That messaging could continue to prove effective. During the midterms, Democratic groups zeroed in on corruption in the White House and sought to connect high gas and grocery prices to a Trump administration they said flouted basic ethical rules while protecting and enriching powerful allies of the president. They connected corruption to the Epstein files, data centers , stock trading and other topics, reinforcing that unscrupulous dealings were at play while costs were going up. Polling obtained by POLITICO in the weeks leading up to Election Day shows the vast majority of Americans — both Democrats and Republicans — say corruption is driving up their costs. And a September poll from Gallup also found about 90 percent of Americans believe corruption is rampant in government. Democrats and several Republicans on Capitol Hill are pushing for more transparency on the extent to which Nvidia’s chips ended up in Chinese hands and further details on Huang’s relationship with suspected spy Alice Huang. “Today's news that Donald Trump engineered the rehiring of Jensen Huang at Nvidia is Exhibit A about the political corruption and rot at the heart of the Trump administration's big tech and AI policy,” Maryland Sen. Chris Van Hollen, who is running to lead Senate Democrats, said in a briefing to reporters. Van Hollen was speculated as a possible 2028 presidential candidate, though he’s now ruled out a White House bid. “We know that President Trump owns Nvidia stock. We know that Jensen Huang contributed to the inauguration, attended a million-dollar plate at Mar-a-Lago and essentially Jensen Huang has been running the Trump administration's AI and big tech policy,” Van Hollen added. Jordain Carney contributed to this report.
authors: By Jason Beeferman and Sam Sutton
